module: Define the release and assessment boundary

lesson.title: Turn requirements into an evidence dossier
lesson.summary: Make a usable evidence matrix and technical-file index.

prerequisites.reason: The dossier must identify which version and system its records describe.
The evidence map must start from the requirements applicable to the chosen route.

blocks: An **evidence matrix** is a practical table linking each applicable requirement to a versioned record, responsible person, demonstrated result, gap and action. The law requires conformity evidence; this table is our review method. A document's existence is not proof that its contents establish conformity.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8–18; Annex IV(1)–(9)

blocks: **Technical documentation** explains the system and demonstrates its requirements. Annex IV(1) covers intended purpose/provider/version, interaction with other software and hardware, versions, market form, hardware, applicable product illustrations, interface and instructions. An index helps a reviewer locate these records for this release.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8–18; Annex IV(1)–(9)

blocks: Annex IV(2) covers development and integration methods, design logic and key choices, architecture and resources, data requirements and governance, human oversight, predetermined changes, validation/testing and cybersecurity. Testing includes datasets, metrics, discriminatory-impact checks where relevant and dated signed reports. Naming a model is not a substitute for these records.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8–18; Annex IV(1)–(9)

blocks: Annex IV(3)–(9) adds detailed monitoring/function/control information; appropriateness of performance metrics; risk-management description; lifecycle changes; applied standards or detailed other compliance solutions; declaration copy; and post-market monitoring system and plan. Annex IV is an index of required substance, not a claim that every sector-law file requirement is taught here.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8–18; Annex IV(1)–(9)

blocks: Northbridge's matrix lists oversight controls, the tested interface version and dated human-review evidence. A blank test report remains a gap even if its index entry exists. Harbour must add the applicable sector-law records; a shared file can be useful, but every required element must still be traceable.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 8–18; Annex IV(1)–(9)

questions.prompt: A matrix links oversight to an empty test-report file. What is the appropriate status?

options.blocks: Evidence gap; obtain and evaluate the test result.
options.reason: The index entry does not establish the control's performance.

options.blocks: Complete because the file has a responsible owner.
options.reason: Responsibility does not replace the missing result.

options.blocks: Complete because oversight appears in the matrix.
options.reason: A listed requirement is not proof of conformity.

questions.prompt: Harbour combines AI and sector records in one dossier. What makes it reviewable?

options.blocks: Use the AI index to dismiss all sector requirements.
options.reason: The relevant sector obligations still need their own evidence.

options.blocks: Trace each applicable requirement to current supporting evidence.
options.reason: Combination is useful only if coverage and gaps remain visible.

options.blocks: Count documents without checking their scope.
options.reason: Volume alone does not establish coverage.
